questions.question: How can we get alerted when one of our production workflows fails?

points.text: Set an error workflow for the workflow in Workflow Settings; it runs when an execution fails (e.g. to send email or Slack alerts).

evidence.quote: For each workflow, you can set an error workflow in Workflow Settings. It runs if an execution fails.

points.text: The error workflow must start with the Error Trigger node.

evidence.quote: The error workflow must start with the Error Trigger.

questions.question: If the trigger node of a workflow is what fails, will the error workflow still receive an execution ID?

points.text: No. execution.id is not present when the error is in the trigger node of the main workflow, because the workflow doesn't execute.

evidence.quote: Not present if the error is in the trigger node of the main workflow, as the workflow doesn't execute.

questions.question: Do we have to build explicit loops so a node processes every item it receives?

points.text: No. Nodes usually run once for each item automatically.

evidence.quote: Nodes usually run once for each item.

points.text: Some nodes are exceptions and need a loop designed in (e.g. Code node in Run Once for All Items mode, HTTP Request pagination).

evidence.quote: Nodes and operations where you need to design a loop into your workflow:
node in Run Once for All Items mode: processes all the items based on the entered code snippet.
you must handle pagination yourself. If your API call returns paginated results you must create a loop to fetch one page at a time.

questions.question: Our API returns paginated results. Will the HTTP Request node fetch all the pages for us?
questions.note: The KB says pagination must be handled by building a loop. Claude may 'know' that newer HTTP Request node versions have a pagination option. The KB-supported answer is what is scored.

points.text: Per the KB, no: with the HTTP Request node you must handle pagination yourself by creating a loop that fetches one page at a time.

evidence.quote: you must handle pagination yourself. If your API call returns paginated results you must create a loop to fetch one page at a time.

questions.question: A node receives many items but we only want it to act on the first one. How?

points.text: Toggle the Execute Once parameter in the node's Settings tab.

evidence.quote: toggling the Execute Once parameter in the Settings tab of that node

questions.question: How should we process a large dataset without hitting an external API's rate limits?

points.text: Use the Loop Over Items node to batch the data and process batches.

evidence.quote: This approach is useful for avoiding API rate limits when processing large incoming data
Use the Loop Over Items node when you want to loop until all items are processed.
You can batch the data in groups and process these batches.

points.text: Add a Wait node between batches to slow processing further.

evidence.quote: Combine batching with a Wait node between batches to slow down processing further.

questions.question: In a workflow that splits into several branches, in what order do the branches run?

points.text: For workflows created from n8n 1.0, each branch runs to completion before the next, ordered top to bottom on the canvas; leftmost first at the same height.

evidence.quote: executes each branch in turn, completing one branch before starting another. n8n orders the branches based on their position on the canvas
If two branches are at the same height, the leftmost branch executes first.

points.text: The execution order can be changed in workflow settings.

evidence.quote: You can change the execution order in your workflow settings.

questions.question: Do sub-workflow executions count toward our plan's monthly execution limit?

points.text: No. Sub-workflow executions don't count towards the monthly execution or active workflow limits.

evidence.quote: Sub-wokflow executions don't count towards your plan's monthly execution or active workflow limits.

questions.question: Can we rely on pinned test data being used when the workflow runs in production?

evidence.quote: Data pinning isn't available for production workflow executions.

evidence.quote: You can't pin data if the output data includes binary data.

questions.question: How much can we store in data tables, and what happens when we hit the limit?

points.text: By default all data tables in an instance share a 200 MiB limit (self-hosted can change it with N8N_DATA_TABLES_MAX_SIZE_BYTES).

evidence.quote: By default, the total storage used by all data tables in an instance is limited to 200 MiB.

points.text: n8n warns at 80% of the limit.

evidence.quote: When your data tables approach 80% of your storage limit, n8n displays a warning.

points.text: Exceeding the limit disables manual additions and causes workflow errors on insert/update.

evidence.quote: Exceeding this limit will disable manual additions to tables and cause workflow execution errors during attempts to insert or update data.

questions.question: Can our Code node read values directly from a data table?

points.text: No. Direct programmatic access to data tables from a Code node isn't supported.

evidence.quote: Direct programmatic access to data tables from a Code node isn't supported.

evidence.quote: the project-scoped variable value takes precedence and overrides the global variable value within that project's workflows.

questions.question: Can we stop a credential from being sent to arbitrary URLs through the HTTP Request node?

None: The credential is blocked entirely from use in the HTTP Request node.
